question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1\,\text{or}\,y<0 \\ \frac{xy-y}{x}, & x\ge 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & x\ge 1,\,y>1.\end{aligned}
$$

Find ${F}_{Y}(y),$ the marginal CDF of $Y,$ for $0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal CDF of $Y$ is given by

$$
{F}_{Y}(y)=F(\infty ,y)={lim}_{x\to \infty }F(x,y).
$$

Therefore, for $0\le y\le 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{xy-y}{x}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{y(x-1)}{x}) \\  & =y{lim}_{x\to \infty }(1-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =y{lim}_{x\to \infty }(1-0) \\  & =y.\end{aligned}
$$
